zh: 」明帝即位，尊后為皇太后，稱永安宮。
literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne he honored the empress as Empress Dowager, with her residence called Yong'an Palace.
idiomatic: When Ming-di succeeded he raised the empress to Empress Dowager of Yong'an Palace.

zh: 太和四年，詔封表安陽亭侯，又進爵鄉侯，增邑並前五百戶，遷中壘將軍。
literal: In the fourth year of Taihe an edict enfeoffed Biao as Marquis of Anyang Pavilion, then advanced his rank to village marquis, added five hundred households to his fief together with what he already held, and transferred him to General of the Central Rampart.
idiomatic: In Taihe 4 an edict made Guo Biao Marquis of Anyang Pavilion, then promoted him to village marquis, added five hundred households to his fief for a total with prior holdings, and appointed him general of the central rampart.

zh: 以表子詳為騎都尉。
literal: He appointed Biao's son Xiang as Cavalry Commandant.
idiomatic: He made Biao's son Guo Xiang cavalry commandant.

zh: 其年，帝追諡太后父永為安陽鄉敬侯，母董為都鄉君。
literal: That year the emperor posthumously honored the empress dowager's father Yong as Marquis Jing of Anyang Village and her mother Dong as Mistress of the Capital Village.
idiomatic: That same year the emperor posthumously ennobled the empress dowager's father Yong as Marquis Jing of Anyang village and her mother Dong as lady of the capital village.

zh: 遷表昭德將軍，加金紫，位特進，表第二子訓為騎都尉。
literal: Biao was transferred to General Who Displays Virtue, given the gold seal and purple ribbon, granted the position of Special Advance, and Biao's second son Xun was made Cavalry Commandant.
idiomatic: Guo Biao was promoted to general who displays virtue, given the gold seal and purple cord and the rank of special advance; Biao's second son Xun became cavalry commandant.

zh: 及孟武母卒，欲厚葬，起祠堂，太后止之曰：「自喪亂以來，墳墓無不發掘，皆由厚葬也；
literal: When Meng Wu's mother died and he wished a lavish burial and to erect an ancestral hall, the empress dowager stopped him, saying, "Since the disorders of war, tombs have all been opened and plundered—all because of lavish burial;
idiomatic: When Meng Wu's mother died and he wanted a lavish funeral and an ancestral shrine, the empress dowager forbade it, saying, "Since the age of chaos no tomb has escaped looting, and lavish burial is always the reason;

zh: 首陽陵可以為法。」
literal: Shouyang Mausoleum may serve as the model."
idiomatic: Take Shouyang Mausoleum as your model."

zh: 青龍三年春，后崩於許昌，以終制營陵，三月庚寅，葬首陽陵西。
literal: In the spring of the third year of Qinglong the empress dowager died at Xuchang; following the final rites a mausoleum was built, and on gengyin in the third month she was buried west of Shouyang Mausoleum.
idiomatic: In the spring of Qinglong 3 the empress dowager died at Xuchang. A tomb was built according to the prescribed mourning rites, and on gengyin of the third month she was buried west of Shouyang Mausoleum.

zh: 《魏略》曰：明帝既嗣立，追痛甄后之薨，故太后以憂暴崩。
literal: The Wei Summary states: Once Emperor Ming had succeeded to the throne and grieved anew for Empress Zhen's death, the empress dowager therefore died suddenly from distress.
idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that once Ming-di had succeeded and was again mourning Empress Wen-Zhao's death, the empress dowager died suddenly of grief.

zh: 甄后臨沒，以帝屬李夫人。
literal: When Empress Zhen was near death she entrusted the emperor to Lady Li.
idiomatic: As Empress Wen-Zhao lay dying she entrusted the emperor to Lady Li.

zh: 及太后崩，夫人乃說甄后見譖之禍，不獲大斂，被髮覆面，帝哀恨流涕，命殯葬太后，皆如甄后故事。
literal: When the empress dowager died Lady Li then told how Empress Zhen had suffered slander and calamity, had not received full encoffinment, and had been left with hair loose and face covered; the emperor mourned and wept in bitter regret and ordered that the empress dowager's funeral and burial follow Empress Zhen's precedent in every respect.
idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, Lady Li recounted how Empress Wen-Zhao had been slandered to her ruin, denied proper encoffinment, and left with hair loose over her face. The emperor wept in grief and rage and ordered the empress dowager's funeral handled exactly as Empress Wen-Zhao's had been.

zh: 漢晉春秋曰：初，甄后之誅，由郭后之寵，及殯，令被髮覆面，以糠塞口，遂立郭后，使養明帝。
literal: Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: At first Empress Zhen's execution came from Empress Guo's favor; at the encoffinment she was made to let her hair hang and cover her face, with chaff stuffed in her mouth; then Empress Guo was established and made to rear Emperor Ming.
idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin records that Empress Wen-Zhao was put to death because of Empress Wen-De's favor; at burial her hair was left loose over her face and chaff was stuffed in her mouth. Empress Wen-De was then enthroned and charged with raising Ming-di.

zh: 帝知之，心常懷忿，數泣問甄后死狀。
literal: The emperor knew this and constantly harbored resentment, weeping again and again as he asked how Empress Zhen had died.
idiomatic: Ming-di knew this and nursed a lasting grievance, weeping repeatedly as he questioned how Empress Wen-Zhao had died.

zh: 郭后曰：「先帝自殺，何以責問我？
literal: Empress Guo said, "The former emperor killed himself—why do you hold me to account?
idiomatic: Empress Wen-De answered, "The late emperor took his own life—why blame me?

zh: 且汝為人子，可追讎死父，為前母枉殺後母邪？」
literal: Moreover, as a son, can you pursue vengeance for a dead father and wrongly kill your stepmother for your former mother?"
idiomatic: And as his son, would you avenge a dead father by killing your stepmother for your birth mother's sake?"

zh: 明帝怒，遂逼殺之，敕殯者使如甄后故事。
literal: Emperor Ming grew angry, then forced her to death, and instructed those handling the encoffinment to follow Empress Zhen's precedent.
idiomatic: Ming-di flew into a rage, forced her to her death, and ordered the embalmers to treat her exactly as Empress Wen-Zhao had been treated.

zh: 《魏書》載哀策曰：「維青龍三年三月壬申，皇太后梓宮啟殯，將葬於首陽之西陵。
literal: The Book of Wei records the lamentation patent, saying, "In the third year of Qinglong, on the third month, day renshen, the empress dowager's coffin was opened for encoffinment and was to be buried at the western mausoleum of Shouyang.
idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves the lamentation patent: "In Qinglong 3, on renshen of the third month, the empress dowager's coffin was opened for burial at the western tomb of Shouyang.

zh: 哀子皇帝叡親奉冊祖載，遂親遣奠，叩心擗踴，號咷仰訴，痛靈魂之遷幸，悲容車之向路，背三光以潛翳，就黃壚而安厝。
literal: The grieving son, Emperor Rui, personally bore the patent and ancestral carriage, then personally sent forth offerings, beating his breast and stamping in grief, wailing and crying heavenward in appeal, pained that the spirit soul was being removed in favor, grieved that the bier was setting out on its road, turning his back on the three luminaries as they dimmed in concealment, and coming to the yellow mound for peaceful rest.
idiomatic: The grieving son, Emperor Rui, personally bore the patent and ancestral carriage, then offered sacrifice himself—beating his breast, stamping in anguish, wailing heavenward—mourning the spirit's departure, grieving the bier's journey, turning from the sun, moon, and stars now dimmed, and committing her to the yellow earth in peace.

zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
literal: Alas, how mournful!
idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

zh: 昔二女妃虞，帝道以彰，三母嬪週，聖善彌光，既多受祉，享國延長。
literal: In antiquity two daughters became consorts of Yu and the imperial way was thereby made manifest; three mothers entered the Zhou house and sagely goodness shone ever brighter; they received abundant blessing and their states endured long.
idiomatic: Long ago two daughters wed into Yu's line and the imperial way shone forth; three mothers entered Zhou and sanctity grew ever brighter—they received great blessing and their realms endured.

zh: 哀哀慈妣，興化閏房，龍飛紫極，作合聖皇，不虞中年，暴罹災殃。
literal: Mournful, mournful is my gracious mother, who raised transforming influence within the inner chambers, rose with the dragon to the purple apex, and was paired with the sage emperor—yet who did not expect mid-life and suddenly met calamity and disaster.
idiomatic: Mournful is my gracious mother, who nurtured virtue in the inner chambers, rose to the purple throne beside the sage emperor, and yet, in mid-life, was suddenly struck by disaster.

zh: 愍予小子，煢煢摧傷，魂雖永逝，定省曷望？
literal: Pity me, this little child, lonely and broken in grief; though the soul has forever departed, how can I still hope for morning and evening attendance?
idiomatic: Pity me, a lonely child crushed with grief; though her soul is gone forever, how can I ever again attend her morning and evening?

zh: 嗚呼哀哉！」
literal: Alas, how mournful!"
idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!"

zh: 帝進表爵為觀津侯，增邑五百，並前千戶。
literal: The emperor advanced Biao's noble rank to Marquis of Guanjin, added five hundred households to his fief, making one thousand together with what he already held.
idiomatic: The emperor promoted Guo Biao to Marquis of Guanjin, added five hundred households to his fief, and brought his total holdings to one thousand households.

zh: 遷詳為駙馬都尉。
literal: Xiang was transferred to Commandant of the Stable for the Son-in-Law.
idiomatic: Guo Xiang was made commandant of the stable for the emperor's son-in-law.

zh: 四年，追改封永為觀津敬侯，世婦董為堂陽君。
literal: In the fourth year Yong was posthumously re-enfeoffed as Marquis Jing of Guanjin and the late wife Dong as Mistress of Tangyang.
idiomatic: In the fourth year Yong was posthumously re-enfeoffed as Marquis Jing of Guanjin and the late wife Dong as lady of Tangyang.

zh: 追封諡后兄浮為梁裡亭戴侯，都為武城亭孝侯，成為新樂亭定侯，皆使使者奉策，祠以太牢。
literal: Posthumously enfeoffing and honoring the empress's elder brothers, Fu was made Marquis Dai of Liangli Pavilion, Du Marquis Xiao of Wucheng Pavilion, and Cheng Marquis Ding of Xinle Pavilion; envoys were sent to each bearing patents, and they were sacrificed to with the grand offering.
idiomatic: The empress dowager's brothers were posthumously ennobled: Fu as Marquis Dai of Liangli pavilion, Du as Marquis Xiao of Wucheng pavilion, and Cheng as Marquis Ding of Xinle pavilion. Envoys were dispatched with patents to sacrifice to each with the grand offering.

zh: 詳薨，子釗嗣。
literal: Xiang died, and his son Zhao succeeded.
idiomatic: Guo Xiang died and was succeeded by his son Zhao.
